<!-- Use this template to propose code improvements that don't change functionality. -->

## Refactoring Target

Which script(s), workflow(s), or codebase area(s) should be refactored?

## Current Issues

What problems exist in the current implementation? Consider:

- Maintainability issues
- Performance bottlenecks
- Code smells or technical debt
- Duplication or redundancy

## Proposed Improvements

Describe the refactoring approach you're suggesting. Be specific about changes where possible.

## Benefits

What benefits will this refactoring provide?

- [ ] Improved maintainability
- [ ] Better performance
- [ ] Reduced complexity
- [ ] Enhanced readability
- [ ] Easier testing
- [ ] Other: **\_**

## Risks and Challenges

What risks or challenges might this refactoring introduce? How can they be mitigated?

## Additional Context

Any other context, code examples, or references that might help.

## Definition of Ready (DoR) Checklist

- [ ] Refactoring target clearly identified
- [ ] Current issues thoroughly described
- [ ] Proposed improvements outlined
- [ ] Benefits and risks assessed
- [ ] Dependencies and impact understood

## Definition of Done (DoD) Checklist (for maintainers)

- [ ] Code refactored as proposed
- [ ] No functional changes introduced
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Code coverage maintained or improved
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Code review completed
- [ ] Performance impact verified (if applicable)
